approval: Two parts proposed in chat on 2026-11-14. (1) Mechanism check: two tuned classical stand-ins for the quantum reservoirs. (2) Classical machine-learning tier: LSTM and GRU on the frequency ladder, raised after the student asked 'are we using any lstm and qlstm'. Student's words: 'add lstm and gru, register together and run'.
extends: long_prereg_dom.json (run 2026-11-13) and long_prereg_dom2.json (run 2026-11-14). Those runs and reports are not changed; their forecasts are READ from long_preds_dom and long_preds_dom2. This is a NEW registration designed AFTER seeing both sets of results, including their held-out scores.
why: After long_prereg_dom2.json two published quantum reservoir designs (DOM = Domingo et al. G3 circuit; ISING = their Ising reservoir) keep a 0.2 to 0.9% gain over a tuned, matched, single-input echo state network at 5 and 15 minutes ('detectable, below band'), none at hourly or daily. Two gaps remain. (a) Nothing shows WHY: the gain could come from the input encoding or from the form of the memory update, both of which can be copied classically. (b) The frequency ladder has no LSTM or GRU, so the 'classical machine learning' tier of the three-tier design (econometric / classical ML / quantum) is only reservoirs and random features there.
questions: Q-M (mechanism): does a classical model that copies the quantum reservoir's input functions, or the algebraic form of its memory update, match DOM and ISING on copper volatility?

Q-T (tiers): on the same rows, how do LSTM and GRU compare with the benchmark, and how do the quantum reservoirs (DOM, ISING, and the project's earlier QRC) compare with LSTM and GRU, at 5 minutes, 15 minutes, hourly and daily?

models.read_not_rerun: DOM, ESN28u (long_preds_dom); ISING, ESN28u_t (long_preds_dom2); QRC = the project's earlier quantum reservoir in its FIXED configuration on H, M, F (long_preds_hf, long_preds_hf2/fixed; the only version stored on all three grids) and QRC_angle (tuned) on D (long_preds_qrc/dbdaily/range; held-out years from long_preds_dom/D_old); benchmark HAR + hour-of-day (H, M, F) or HARq (D).
models.ESNq_t: dom3_lib.esn_k: the 28-unit leaky echo state network of ESN28u_t with TWO inputs, the input functions through which u enters the quantum reservoir: u (standardised; identical to the ESN28u input) and sqrt(u(1-u)) (standardised with training rows). Input scale 0.5. 12 configurations: spectral radius {0.6, 0.9, 1.2} x leak {0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0}. Tests whether the encoding's input functions explain the gain.
models.SAS28_t: dom3_lib.sas: state-affine system with a 28-number state, s_t = (1-leak) s_{t-1} + leak (A(u_t) s_{t-1} + b(u_t)), A(u) = (1-u) A0 + u A1 + sqrt(u(1-u)) A2 and the same form for b; A_i random Gaussian scaled to spectral norm 'gain', b_i uniform on (-1,1); features = the 28 state numbers. No tanh. This is the algebraic form of the quantum reservoir's memory update (the 6-qubit memory is updated by a map that is linear in the state with exactly these three coefficients), with a small classical state in place of the 64 x 64 density matrix. 12 configurations: gain {0.3, 0.5, 0.65} x leak {0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0} (gain <= 0.65 keeps the update a contraction). Tests whether 'the input multiplies the memory' explains the gain.
models.standin_tuning_and_readout: As ESN28u_t in long_prereg_dom2.json: intraday, configuration chosen by validation mean squared error with tuning seeds 100, 101; daily, by validation QLIKE with tuning seeds 100-102; then seeds 0-9, forecasts averaged. Readouts unchanged (intraday: ridge on 28 features fitted to the benchmark residual; daily: HAR features + 28 features, linear QLIKE model).
models.LSTM_GRU_intraday: dom3_lib.Net + fit_seq: one recurrent layer (LSTM or GRU) and a linear head on the last hidden state. Input: the last 10 bins of 5 channels (return, ln RV, ln volume, hour sine, hour cosine), standardised with training rows; this is the window the stored ESN reads. Target: benchmark residual divided by its training standard deviation; forecast = benchmark + network output. Adam, squared error, batch 512, at most 30 epochs, early stopping on validation (patience 4). 12 configurations: hidden {8, 16, 32} x learning rate {3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2}, chosen by validation MSE with ONE tuning seed (100); then seeds 0-9, forecasts averaged.
models.LSTM_GRU_daily: dom3_lib.fit_daily, following long_nn.py / v2_nn.train_net: last 5 days of the three standardised HAR inputs (lvR1, lvR5, lvR22); eta = lvR5 + network output; QLIKE loss; Adam, batch 32, at most 25 epochs, patience 5. Same 12 configurations, chosen by validation QLIKE with tuning seeds 100-102; then seeds 0-9, level forecasts averaged, validation-calibrated scale in the report.
models.everything_else: Rows, targets, splits, purge, benchmark, input series and scaling exactly as long_prereg_dom.json (dom3_run.py keeps the row-building code of dom2_run.py unchanged; checked by diff). dom3_report.py stops if rows, targets or benchmark forecasts differ between any of the stored files.
models.not_included: QLSTM is NOT run: training a simulated quantum circuit on 60,000 to 190,000 rows per block is not feasible here. The paper reports the QLSTM from the earlier long-daily and 2020-2026 hourly runs, with the block difference stated.

input_differences: Not like for like, and stated wherever family T is reported: LSTM and GRU read 5 channels x 10 bins (intraday) or 3 HAR inputs x 5 days (daily); QRC reads 8 inputs (6 on D); DOM, ISING, ESN28u_t, ESNq_t, SAS28_t read ONE series recurrently. Family T therefore compares model tiers as they would be used, not a quantum-versus-classical mechanism. Family M is the like-for-like comparison (same single series, 28 features, same readout).
blocks: As long_prereg_dom.json: intraday H, M, F test years 2013-2025 (13 blocks each); daily D test years 2015-2024; held-out intraday 2026 and daily 2025, 2026, run after the rolling report is written.
statistics: As long_prereg_dom2.json (loss, HAC interval, lags H 24 / M 96 / F 288 / D 10, +/-3% band, verdict words, size categories, Holm within family and stratum, regimes). Families: M mechanism (Holm over 4) = DOM vs ESNq_t, DOM vs SAS28_t, ISING vs ESNq_t, ISING vs SAS28_t; T quantum vs classical ML (Holm over 6) = DOM, ISING, QRC each vs LSTM and vs GRU; L classical ML vs benchmark (Holm over 3) = LSTM vs benchmark, GRU vs benchmark, LSTM vs GRU; C descriptive = ESNq_t vs ESN28u_t, SAS28_t vs ESN28u_t, ESNq_t vs benchmark, SAS28_t vs benchmark, LSTM vs ESN28u_t, GRU vs ESN28u_t, DOM vs ESN28u_t, ISING vs ESN28u_t (the last two repeat long_prereg_dom2.json for reference).
size_categories: As long_prereg_dom2.json, printed for families M, T, L: 'meaningful edge' = Holm p < 0.05 and whole 95% interval below 0.97; 'detectable, below band' = Holm p < 0.05 and whole interval below 1 but not below 0.97; 'detectably worse' = Holm p < 0.05 and whole interval above 1; otherwise 'no detectable difference'.

decision_rules.mechanism: Per grid and per quantum reservoir (DOM, ISING), pooled over all blocks: 'explained by a classical stand-in' if against AT LEAST ONE of ESNq_t, SAS28_t the category is 'no detectable difference' or 'detectably worse'; 'not explained' if it is 'detectable, below band' or 'meaningful edge' against BOTH. The rule is informative only where a gap over ESN28u_t existed (M and F rolling; M and F held-out); on other grids it is printed but there was nothing to explain.
decision_rules.what_not_explained_means: 'Not explained' means only that these two 28-feature stand-ins do not reproduce the gain. It does NOT show a quantum advantage: the gain is below the +/-3% band, the simulation is itself a classical computation, and larger or other classical models are not excluded.
decision_rules.tiers: Reported per grid as categories. A quantum model is said to beat the classical ML tier on a grid only with a 'meaningful edge' over the better of LSTM and GRU (lower pooled loss). 'Detectably worse' is reported as such. Because inputs differ (see input_differences) no mechanism claim follows.
decision_rules.classical_ML_tier: LSTM or GRU is said to improve on the econometric benchmark on a grid with 'meaningful edge'; 'detectable, below band' is reported as a small gain of no practical size.
decision_rules.heldout: Same categories on held-out data, one stratum, read together with the rolling result.

student_prediction.reading: NOT stated. The student was asked 'will a classical stand-in match the quantum reservoir?' and answered 'add lstm and gru, register together and run'. Left null.

claude_prediction_recorded_for_transpare.text: Mechanism: the stand-ins close part of the gap but not all of it. ESNq_t is within 0.1% of ESN28u_t; SAS28_t is worse than ESN28u_t. So 'not explained' on F rolling for both reservoirs (the sample is very large), and mixed on M. Tiers: LSTM and GRU beat the benchmark by about 1 to 3% on H, M, F ('detectable, below band') and are 'no detectable difference' or worse on D; DOM and ISING are 'detectably worse' than the networks on M and F because the networks read five channels; QRC is within 1% of the networks. No 'meaningful edge' for any quantum model. My two earlier predictions in this series were wrong, so this one deserves little weight.

checks_done_before_registration: Nothing scored. (1) dom3_lib.selftest on random numbers: both stand-ins give 28 finite, input-responsive features and forget their start; LSTM and GRU learn a planted signal. (2) fit_daily on synthetic numbers beats the anchor for LSTM and GRU. (3) dom3_run.py H 2015 with DRY=1: shapes only (3000 bins, one epoch on 2000 rows, no forecast kept). (4) diff: the row-building section of dom3_run.py is identical to dom2_run.py. (5) dom3_report.py comparison, Holm and category functions on synthetic numbers. (6) Timing on random numbers: 1 to 2.6 s per epoch of 186,000 rows; stand-ins 4 to 10 microseconds per step. dom3_daily.py was NOT executed before registration (it has no dry mode).
known_limits: Designed after seeing all results of long_prereg_dom.json and long_prereg_dom2.json, including held-out 2025-26. The held-out period is unseen only for the four new models.

The stand-ins are two designs chosen by the author. SAS28_t has a 28-number state; the quantum memory is a 64 x 64 density matrix read through 28 numbers. A larger classical state is not tested, so 'not explained' is weak evidence.

LSTM and GRU: one layer, small widths, one tuning seed intraday, 12 configurations, no dropout or weight decay, CPU training. A larger search could change small differences. Networks read more inputs than the single-input reservoirs.
QRC on H, M, F is the fixed (untuned) configuration; tuned QRC exists only on H and M and is not used, to keep the grids comparable.
No QLSTM on the ladder (see not_included).

All limits of long_prereg_dom.json and long_prereg_dom2.json remain: authors' designs on a different task, two circuit details and two Ising details are my reading of the preprint, min-max scaling, exact simulation, copper only, overlapping blocks, narrow HAC intervals at intraday sample sizes, AI-written code not re-derived by the student, licensed data not committed.
cost_estimate: From timings on random numbers: a 5-minute block needs 44 network fits of at most 30 epochs (worst case about 1 hour, typically less) plus about 3 minutes for the stand-ins. With eight jobs side by side: roughly 1.5 to 3 hours in total. The two earlier estimates in this series were off by up to 60%. No hardware jobs; no new data.
stop_rule: One run of the registered jobs (39 intraday and 10 daily rolling blocks, then 5 held-out jobs), report and stop. No new models, grids, seeds, stand-ins or categories after results. A crashed job is re-run unchanged.
